It’s the Lag Ba’Omer holiday too. It’s fine.” It was dark, and we were all still asleep when Dad woke me up. “Brush your teeth, Zevik.” “What about everyone else?” I asked. “You’re the only one coming,” Dad replied. He was thirty-five, thirty-five years old. Where was I at thirty-five? The First Lebanon War. Five wars later. I sat in the jeep on the right side. The red of the poppies and the yellow of the chrysanthemums gave way to the pink of flax and the blue of cornflowers.
